arxiv-2201-08920.title: The free-energy landscape of a mechanically bistable DNA origami
arxiv-2201-08920.creator: Chak Kui Wong, Jonathan P. K. Doye
arxiv-2201-08920.description: Abstract Molecular simulations using coarse-grained models allow the structure, dynamics and mechanics of DNA origamis to be comprehensively characterized. Here, we focus on the free-energy landscape of a jointed DNA origami that has been designed to exhibit two mechanically stable states and for which a bistable landscape has been inferred from ensembles of structures visualized by electron microscopy.

arxiv-2212-02683.title: A Visually Classified Spectroscopic Object Catalog for SDSS-IV MaNGA
arxiv-2212-02683.creator: Joshua L. Steffen, Hai Fu
arxiv-2212-02683.description: Abstract We provide a catalog of visually classified objects in the MaNGA integral field spectroscopic survey. The MaNGA survey is designed to target a single galaxy with each of its integral field units (IFUs); however, many of these fields will host ancillary objects. We identify these discrete objects by cleaning up SDSS photometric objects in MaNGA’s fields-of-view.

arxiv-2302-06663.title: Mergers of neutron stars and black holes with cores of giant stars: a population synthesis study
arxiv-2302-06663.creator: Aldana Grichener
arxiv-2302-06663.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Aldana Grichener. We perform population synthesis of massive binaries to study the mergers of neutron stars (NSs) and black holes (BHs) with the cores of their giant secondaries during common envelope evolution (CEE). We use different values of the efficiency parameter α CE \alpha_{\rm CE} in the framework of the energy formalism for traditional CEE ( α CE ≤ 1 \alpha_{\rm CE}\leq 1 ) and including additional energy sources to unbind the envelope ( α CE > 1 \alpha_{\rm CE}>1 ).

arxiv-2304-06816.title: Quantum dust cores of black holes
arxiv-2304-06816.creator: Roberto Casadio
arxiv-2304-06816.description: Abstract We describe the ground state for a gravitationally collapsed ball of dust as the direct product of wavefunctions for dust particles distributed over an arbitrary number of nested layers. This allows us to estimate the expectation value of the global radius as well as the effective energy density and pressures for the dust core of quantum black holes.

arxiv-2307-02918.title: Does personality affect the allocation of resources within households? Ph.D. student at the University of Leuven (KU Leuven), Department of Economics, Naamsestraat 69, box 3565, 3000 Leuven (e-mail: gfernandez@kuleuven.be). I deeply appreciate the invaluable guidance of my advisors Laurens Cherchye
arxiv-2307-02918.creator: [Version: August 9, 2026]
arxiv-2307-02918.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by [Version: August 9, 2026]. This paper examines whether personality influences the allocation of resources within households. To do so, I model households as couples who make Pareto-efficient allocations and divide resources according to a distribution function. Using a sample of Dutch couples from the LISS survey with detailed information on consumption, labor supply, and personality traits at the individual level, I find that personality affects intrahousehold allocations through two channels.

arxiv-2312-15992.title: The galaxy bispectrum in the Spherical Fourier-Bessel basis
arxiv-2312-15992.creator: Joshua N. Benabou, Adriano Testa, Chen Heinrich, Henry S. Grasshorn Gebhardt, Olivier Doré
arxiv-2312-15992.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Joshua N. Benabou, Adriano Testa, Chen Heinrich, Henry S. Grasshorn Gebhardt, Olivier Doré. The bispectrum, the three-point correlation in Fourier space, is a crucial statistic for studying many effects targeted by the next-generation galaxy surveys, such as primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) and general relativistic (GR) effects on large scales.

arxiv-2403-16992.title: Complex-Valued Signal Recovery using the Bayesian LASSO This work is partially supported by NSF DMS grant #1912685, AFOSR grant #F9550-22-1-0411, DOE ASCR grant #DE-ACO5-000R22725, and DoD ONR MURI grant #N00014-20-1-2595.
arxiv-2403-16992.creator: Dylan Green, Jonathan Lindbloom, Anne Gelb
arxiv-2403-16992.description: Abstract Recovering complex-valued image recovery from noisy indirect data is important in applications such as ultrasound imaging and synthetic aperture radar. While there are many effective algorithms to recover point estimates of the magnitude, fewer are designed to recover the phase. Quantifying uncertainty in the estimate can also provide valuable information for real-time decision making.

arxiv-2410-08322.title: Extendibility of fermionic states and rigorous ground state approximations of interacting fermionic systems
arxiv-2410-08322.creator: Christian Krumnow, Zoltán Zimborás, Jens Eisert
arxiv-2410-08322.description: Abstract Solving interacting fermionic quantum many-body problems as they are ubiquitous in quantum chemistry and materials science is a central task of theoretical and numerical physics, a task that can commonly only be addressed in the sense of providing approximations of ground states.

arxiv-2505-07588.title: Extremal Cat Herding
arxiv-2505-07588.creator: Rylo Ashmore, Danny Dyer, Rebecca Milley
arxiv-2505-07588.description: Abstract The game of Cat Herding is one in which cat and herder players alternate turns, with the evasive cat moving along non-trivial paths between vertices, and the herder deleting single edges from the graph. Eventually the cat cannot move, and the number of edges deleted is the cat number of the graph.

arxiv-2601-19926.title: The Grammar of Transformers: A Systematic Review of Interpretability Research on Syntactic Knowledge in Language Models
arxiv-2601-19926.creator: Nora Graichen, Iria de-Dios-Flores, Gemma Boleda, Universitat Pompeu Fabra, ICREA*Equal senior authorship. nora.graichen@upf.edu
arxiv-2601-19926.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Nora Graichen, Iria de-Dios-Flores, Gemma Boleda, Universitat Pompeu Fabra, ICREA*Equal senior authorship. nora.graichen@upf.edu. We present a systematic review of 337 articles evaluating the syntactic abilities of Transformer-based language models, reporting on 1,015 model results from a range of syntactic phenomena and interpretability methods.

britannica-1911-catechism.title: Catechism (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-catechism.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-catechism.description: Article 'Catechism' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 5), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The catechism as we know it is intended primarily for children and uneducated persons. Its aim is to instruct, and it differs from a creed or confession in not being in the first instance an act of worship or a public profession of belief. The first regular catechisms seem to have grown out of the usual oral teaching of catechumens, and to have been compiled in the 8th and 9th centuries.

europmc-pmc3260807.creator: Chappell WH, Steelman LS, Long JM, Kempf RC, Abrams SL, Franklin RA, Bäsecke J, Stivala F, Donia M, Fagone P, Malaponte G, Mazzarino MC, Nicoletti F, Libra M, Maksimovic-Ivanic D, Mijatovic S, Montalto G, Cervello M, Laidler P, Milella M, Tafuri A, Bonati A, Evangelisti C, Cocco L, Martelli AM, McCubrey JA.

One of the main ACT approaches is chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy. CAR T cells mediate MHC-unrestricted tumor cell killing by enabling

pmc-10573346.title: Dissolution Behavior of Lime with Different Properties into Converter Slag
pmc-10573346.creator: Mengxu Zhang, Jianli Li, Cao Jia, Yue Yu
pmc-10573346.description: China’s 2022 crude steel production soared to an impressive 1.018 billion tons, and steel slag constituted approximately 10% to 15% of this massive output. However, a notable hindrance to the comprehensive utilization of steel slag arises from the fact that it contains 10% to 20% of free calcium oxide (f-CaO), resulting in volume instability.

pmc-10647810.title: Bridging Neuroscience and Robotics: Spiking Neural Networks in Action
pmc-10647810.creator: Alexander Jones, Vaibhav Gandhi, Adam Y Mahiddine, Christian Huyck, Diego R Faria, Alessandro Carfì, Timothy Patten, Markus Vincze
pmc-10647810.description: Robots are becoming increasingly sophisticated in the execution of complex tasks. However, an area that requires development is the ability to act in dynamically changing environments. To advance this, developments have turned towards understanding the human brain and applying this to improve robotics.

pmc-11516416.title: School-based outdoor education and teacher well-being: the LärMiljö (Learning Environment) - study
pmc-11516416.creator: N Simonsen, N Wackström, J Ray
pmc-11516416.description: BackgroundSchool-based outdoor education (OE) is a teaching method aiming to promote pupils’ learning and wellbeing. OE with its action-oriented and cooperative learning approach can inspire teachers to develop their teaching and may also have a positive impact on their work wellbeing.

pmc-11545856.title: Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Surgery in Elderly Patients: Results from a Multicenter Study
pmc-11545856.creator: Alessandra Francica, Cristina Barbero, Filippo Tonelli, Alfredo Giuseppe Cerillo, Vittoria Lodo, Paolo Centofanti, Giovanni Marchetto, Germano Di Credico, Ruggero De Paulis, Pierluigi Stefano, Giovanni Battista Luciani, Francesco Onorati, Mauro Rinaldi
pmc-11545856.description: Background: Minimally invasive mitral valve surgery (MIMVS) has been increasingly adopted worldwide as an alternative to conventional sternotomy, especially for young patients. The remarkable results gained by MIMVS have encouraged its application in more complex and fragile patients, such as the elderly, though results in this subgroup remain controversial.

pmc-11672969.title: State of Knowledge About Thyroid Cancers in the Era of COVID-19—A Narrative Review
pmc-11672969.creator: Agnieszka Bronowicka-Szydełko, Maciej Rabczyński, Ilias Dumas, Żanna Fiodorenko-Dumas, Beata Wojtczak, Łukasz Kotyra, Irena Kustrzeba-Wójcicka, Łukasz Lewandowski, Beata Ponikowska, Aleksandra Kuzan, Joanna Kluz, Andrzej Gamian, Katarzyna Madziarska, Santiago Garcia-Vallve
pmc-11672969.description: Thyroid cancer (TC), due to its heterogeneous nature, remains a clinical challenge. Many factors can initiate the carcinogenesis process of various types of TC, which complicates diagnosis and treatment. The presented review gathers current information on specific types of TC, taking into account the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12416687.title: Unveiling the mechanism of Pogostemon cablin (Blanco) Benth in treating heat illnesses via network pharmacology and molecular simulation
pmc-12416687.creator: Xiang Li, Sishi Jiang, Haili Li, Shilin Li, Yingchun Hu
pmc-12416687.description: BackgroundHeat illness is a dangerous condition marked by a widespread inflammatory response. Although Pogostemon cablin (Blanco) Benth and its derivatives are clinically used, their mechanisms remain unclear.Methods11 heat illness patients and 14 healthy volunteers from Southwest Medical University Affiliated Hospital were enrolled. Bulk RNA sequencing of peripheral blood samples identified disease-relevant modules via weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA).

pmc-12567033.title: Molecular Transmission Network and Pretreatment Drug Resistance of Newly Diagnosed HIV-1 Infections in Taizhou, a Coastal City in Eastern China, from 2021–2023
pmc-12567033.creator: Junxiao Lin, Haijiang Lin, Guixia Li, Shanling Wang, Tingting Wang, Qiguo Meng, Tingting Hua, Yali Xie, Jiafeng Zhang, Weiwei Shen
pmc-12567033.description: Objective: This study conducted a comprehensive analysis of molecular transmission networks and pretreatment drug resistance (PDR) in newly diagnosed HIV-1 infections in Taizhou, China. Methods: From 2021 to 2023, we collected 1126 plasma samples from newly diagnosed HIV patients in Taizhou.

pmc-12594871.title: Advanced optical measurement techniques for simultaneous fibre orientation and flow analysis complemented by machine learning
pmc-12594871.creator: Tim Vaupel, Florian Gerland, Thomas Schomberg, Olaf Wünsch
pmc-12594871.description: A new measuring method is presented that allows time-resolved quasi-simultaneous measurement of fibre orientation and flow velocity of a transparent fluid such as a substitute fluid for fresh concrete or polymer melt, thus enabling the flow-related fibre orientation process to be visualised and thus better understood.

pmc-12748289.title: Threshold effects of physical activity and cognitive function among older adults with diabetes mellitus in NHANES 2011–2014
pmc-12748289.creator: Jigang Ren, Huibiao Li, Li Liufu, YuPing Yang, Danting Long, Hong Liu, Lidian Chen
pmc-12748289.description: BackgroundDeterioration of cognitive function with aging is a significant public health issue, particularly in individuals with diabetes mellitus (DM). Exercise has been shown to enhance cognitive function. However, the threshold effect of physical activity on cognitive function in older adult people with DM remains unclear.

pmc-13096237.title: Driving sustainable innovation outcomes through employee AI collaboration with the mediating role of sustainable career capacities
pmc-13096237.creator: Zenglin Wu, Hong Gan, Luxin Zhang, Wan Mohd Hirwani Wan Hussain, Sawal Hamid Md Ali
pmc-13096237.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Amid digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI) integration into organizational work has reshaped employee-technology interactions and career trajectories. Despite growing interest in Employee-AI Collaboration (EAC), there is little research examining its impact on both sustainable career development and innovation outcomes. Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and Social Cognitive Theory (SCT), this study examines how EAC influences Sustainable Innovation Outcomes (SIO) via Sustainable Career (SC) capacities and the moderating effect of Self-Efficacy in Using AI (SEUA).

pmc-13138281.title: Sleep-Related Problems and Problematic Smartphone Use in Young Adult Males: Findings from a Short-Term Behavioral Restriction Study
pmc-13138281.creator: Özge Özen Gökmuharremoğlu, Aysel Çoban Taşkın
pmc-13138281.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeProblematic smartphone use is a prevalent behavioral issue in the digital age and is frequently associated with sleep disturbances. However, evidence on how different sleep domains respond to short-term behavioral restriction under natural conditions remains limited.

pmc-13204647.title: Phosphorylated Alpha-Synuclein and Carboxymethyllysine in the Epidermis of Type 2 Diabetes Patients: Preliminary Observations
pmc-13204647.creator: Bernard Kordas, Wojciech Matuszewski, Robert Modzelewski, Judyta Juranek
pmc-13204647.description: Background/objectives: Alpha-synuclein (aSyn) is best known for its role in Parkinson’s disease. Increasing evidence suggests a bidirectional relationship between diabetes mellitus and synuclein pathology. Carboxymethyllysine (CML), an advanced glycation end-product, serves as a marker of cumulative glycation stress and tissue damage in diabetes.

pmc-13211599.title: Speech Recognition–Based Dietary Assessment Tool for Older Adults: Validation and Usability Study
pmc-13211599.creator: Yoonjee ‍Sung, Soyoung Jung, Hae Jin Kang, So Young Moon, Jee Hyang Jeong, Seong Hye Choi, Eun-Hye Lee, Yoo Kyoung Park, Angely Garcia
pmc-13211599.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAs populations age globally, accurate and feasible dietary assessment for older adults has become increasingly important. South Korea has already become an “aged society,” with over 14.2% of its population being aged 65 years and older, and is projected to become one of the world’s most rapidly super-aged societies by 2050, with more than 40% of its population in this age group.

pmc-13234943.title: Preventive service use among Medicaid expansion adults, 2014–2019
pmc-13234943.creator: Michelle Bronsard, Sarah Hirsch, Dawn Pepin, Terrika Barham, Angela T Estadt, Michelle Van Handel, Joshua A Salomon, Adrienne Sabety
pmc-13234943.description: IntroductionIn 2014, the Affordable Care Act (ACA) mandated that newly eligible Medicaid expansion beneficiaries receive recommended preventive services at no cost. Yet, evidence regarding the Medicaid expansion population's use of preventive services is limited.MethodsMedicaid claims data from 2011 to 2019. We focused on 12 selected preventive services that received new, revised, or upheld A or B USPSTF ratings since 2010.

pmc-13302039.title: Individual patterns of stable high-rate activity during atrial fibrillation are determined by local slow-conduction and predict arrhythmia recurrence - insights from non-invasive global mapping
pmc-13302039.creator: A Victor, A Rodriguez, I Llorente, A Costafreda, E Arbelo, A Porta-Sanchez, J M Tolosana, E Guasch, A M Climent, G Hindricks, I Roca-Luque, L Mont, T F Althoff
pmc-13302039.description: BackgroundWith long-term recurrence rates over 50% after catheter ablation, atrial fibrillation (AF) therapy is still not satisfactory. One likely reason is our limited understanding of individual AF mechanisms. This in turn, is in part owed to the absence of mapping systems that are capable of assessing the spatio-temporal AF dynamics in a global, beat-to-beat fashion.

pmc-13534858.title: From Recommendation to Reality
pmc-13534858.creator: Darshali A. Vyas, Sean D. Levy
pmc-13534858.description: ese changes, race-neutral Global Lung Initiative (GLI) Global equations for interpreting pulmonary function tests (PFTs)3 pose unique implementation challenges. Unlike web-based risk scores like the new PREVENT calculator or revised Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC) calculator that lend themselves to immediate online updates,2 changes to PFT interpretation fundamentally alter how we evaluate organ function and understand patients’ lung health.

pmc-13676602.title: Effects of electrical stimulation on the cardiogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells: A systematic review
pmc-13676602.creator: Alejandra Sandoval Villarreal, Paola Neuta-Arciniegas, John Jairo Cabrera-López, Álvaro José Rojas Arciniegas
pmc-13676602.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electrical stimulation has emerged as a promising strategy for promoting cardiogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells; however, the available evidence remains highly heterogeneous across stimulation parameters, experimental platforms, and outcome measures. This systematic review synthesized the available in vitro evidence regarding the effects of electrical stimulation on MSC cardiogenic differentiation, with particular emphasis on stimulation parameters, experimental platforms and biological outcomes related to early cardiogenic commitment and structural maturation.
